question: How many total blood vessels are typically found inside a normal term umbilical cord?
explanation: A healthy term umbilical cord contains three vessels, consisting of two arteries and one single vein. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T3#BMP210_U5_T3_h1)

question: What is the primary function of the umbilical vein in fetal circulation?

options.A: Pumping deoxygenated blood away from the fetal heart
options.B: Carrying oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus
options.C: Providing structural support to keep the cord from twisting
options.D: Transporting fetal waste products directly to the maternal kidneys

explanation: Unlike adult veins, the fetal umbilical vein carries freshly oxygenated blood and essential nutrients from the placental bed straight to the developing baby. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T3#BMP210_U5_T3_h1)

question: What is the main substance that gives Wharton's jelly its soft, cushion-like feel?
explanation: Wharton's jelly is made of a specialized mucous connective tissue rich in mucopolysaccharides that creates a protective gel. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T3#BMP210_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why is Wharton's jelly so important for the baby during labor?

options.A: It prevents the umbilical blood vessels from collapsing when compressed
options.B: It actively pumps oxygen directly into the fetal bloodstream
options.C: It attaches the placenta securely to the upper uterine wall
options.D: It neutralizes toxins present in the amniotic fluid

explanation: The jelly acts as a natural shock absorber, shielding the fragile blood vessels from closing off as the uterus tightens during contractions. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T3#BMP210_U5_T3_h2)

question: What does a single umbilical artery mean for the structure of the cord?

options.A: All three normal vessels have fused into a single tube
options.B: The cord contains two veins and no arteries at all
options.C: The umbilical vein has split into two separate channels
options.D: Only one artery is present alongside one vein

explanation: A single umbilical artery means the cord has a total of two vessels instead of the normal three. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T3#BMP210_U5_T3_h3)

question: A baby is born with a single umbilical artery. What should the midwife check for next?

options.A: Emergency histological culture of the placenta
options.B: Immediate surgical repair of the uterus
options.C: Emergency intravenous antibiotics for the infant
options.D: Associated organ issues like kidney or heart defects

explanation: Because a single umbilical artery is sometimes linked with internal organ malformations, checking for renal and cardiac issues is an important follow-up step. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T3#BMP210_U5_T3_h3)

question: What condition describes an umbilical cord wrapped around the neck of the fetus?
explanation: When the umbilical cord loops around the fetal neck during gestation or delivery, it is clinically termed a nuchal cord. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T3#BMP210_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why can an unusually long umbilical cord be risky during labor?

options.A: It prevents the amniotic fluid from forming properly
options.B: It increases the likelihood of cord prolapse and knot formation
options.C: It stops the fetus from moving its limbs entirely
options.D: It automatically causes complete failure of the placenta

explanation: Extra cord length gives the baby more room to slip through loops, making dangerous tangles, true knots, and prolapse much more likely. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T3#BMP210_U5_T3_h4)

question: Where does the umbilical cord attach in a battledore placenta?

options.A: Directly into the center of the maternal myometrium
options.B: Freely floating within the lower uterine segment
options.C: At the extreme margin or edge of the placenta
options.D: Through the membranes far away from the placental disk

explanation: In a battledore insertion, the cord attaches at the margin or edge of the placental mass rather than the center. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T3#BMP210_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why is a velamentous cord insertion risky when the waters break?

options.A: The exposed vessels lack Wharton's jelly protection and can easily tear
options.B: The placenta will instantly detach from the uterine wall
options.C: The umbilical vein will permanently close and stop all blood flow
options.D: The amniotic fluid will turn toxic upon contact with the air

explanation: In a velamentous insertion, vessels travel unprotected across the membranes, making them vulnerable to tearing and severe bleeding when the membranes rupture. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T3#BMP210_U5_T3_h5)

question: What is the first critical action a midwife must take if an umbilical cord prolapses?

options.A: Administer oxytocin infusion to speed up the normal vaginal delivery
options.B: Manually push the presenting part upward to relieve pressure off the cord
options.C: Instruct the mother to stand up and walk around to reposition the baby
options.D: Wait patiently for natural cervical dilation to complete on its own

explanation: Relieving pressure on the prolapsed cord by elevating the fetal part is the single most important step to prevent oxygen loss while preparing for delivery. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T3#BMP210_U5_T3_h6)

question: Which fetal heart rate pattern on the monitor is typically linked with cord compression?
explanation: Sudden drops in the fetal heart rate that vary in timing with contractions usually point to temporary compression of the umbilical cord. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T3#BMP210_U5_T3_h6)
